blocks.text: Beth-shean appears in verse 12 as part of the administrative region assigned to Baana. Archaeological excavations at the site reveal inscriptions, architecture, pottery, and administrative remains that provide material evidence for understanding major centers in the ancient Near East during this period and help contextualize the administrative infrastructure described in the biblical text.

The archaeological record at Beth-shean documents it as a major regional center whose significance persisted across successive imperial transitions. This continuity of importance at the site through different periods of imperial rule demonstrates Beth-shean's sustained strategic and administrative value within the broader Levantine sphere.
